title: Explain missing observations
summary: Missing data should not be silently shown as a real zero. A gap can honestly show that no observation was recorded.
introduction: Missing data should not be silently shown as a real zero. A gap can honestly show that no observation was recorded. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Missing data should not be silently shown as a real zero. A gap can honestly show that no observation was recorded.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, float("nan"), 4], marker="o")
plt.show()
blocks.title: Explain missing observations

blocks.text: The missing middle value breaks the line. It is not plotted as zero.

blocks.text: Filling missing data requires a justified choice, not a convenient visual shortcut.
